mechanism_narrative: The ongoing collapse in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals fewer discretionary trips to commercial areas, so RETAIL_REC will stay lower than in the previous four weeks over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not recover for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 percent for a week or more, household substitution to at-home routines suppresses retail visits with a one-week lag, pushing RETAIL_REC down further.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL crosses above 20 and remains above 20 for at least 7 days
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next week despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +20 throughout that week.

mechanism_narrative: A joint decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES below their recent lows indicates commuting suppression is still intensifying, and that combined shock will keep retail-and-recreation mobility falling over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -70 and WORKPLACES falls below -50 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline further even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below the stated thresholds for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains less negative than RETAIL_REC by more than 25 points, shopping is being compressed into essential trips only, which will continue to pull down retail-and-recreation mobility within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds RETAIL_REC by more than 25 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds while the gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC stays above 25 points for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility during the week after a sharp trough indicates substitution toward outdoor recreation, and that substitution will partially lift retail-and-recreation mobility over the following month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points from its prior week after a trough below -50
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds from a trough but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises while TRANSIT falls in the same week, people are reallocating time away from external trips, and that cross-signal predicts a further drop in retail-and-recreation mobility within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week even though RESIDENTIAL increases and TRANSIT decreases in the same observation window.

mechanism_narrative: During tightening restrictions, a sustained drop in WORKPLACES below -50 means nonessential activity is still being suppressed, and retail-and-recreation mobility will continue to deteriorate over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next month while WORKPLACES stays below -50 for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT keeps falling faster than PARKS rise, the city is losing commuter-generated foot traffic without fully replacing it with outdoor activity, so RETAIL_REC will remain below its recent average over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT declines by at least 5 points week-on-week while PARKS does not rise by at least 5 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises despite continued TRANSIT deterioration and no comparable PARKS rebound.
